How to use this calculator

  1. Enter initial quantity, half-life duration, elapsed duration.
  2. Select Calculate to see the answer and its breakdown.
  3. Keep a scenario, change an input and compare the results.

Use consistent units and check the assumptions below before applying the result.

How half-life is calculated

Remaining amount = initial amount × (1/2)^(elapsed time / half-life). This continuous model works for any nonnegative elapsed duration; it does not predict individual decay events. After three half-lives, 80 mg becomes 80 × (1/2)³ = 10 mg.

Remaining quantity = initial×(1/2)^(elapsed/half-life).
A worked example

After three half-lives, 80 mg becomes 80 × (1/2)³ = 10 mg.

Assumptions & useful context

The result depends on the values you enter and the method described above. Displayed numbers may be rounded; calculations use the unrounded values. Check that this model matches your situation before relying on it.

Frequently asked questions

Does one half-life mean all material disappears?

No. It means the expected quantity is reduced by half.

Does the output account for environmental conditions?

No; it assumes the supplied half-life is constant and the system is not replenished.
